Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE RESULT the guess is about: At lc.queue.parts.fa=0.179, p0179_len1000 r009 has fb_loss_frac=0.090105 versus p0179 r005 fb_loss_frac=0.098561, a 0.008456 reduction, while fa_goodput_bps=25394445 and fb_goodput_bps=72114560 are unchanged; C7 and V7 support that lc.queue.length=1000 did not raise fa_goodput_bps by more than 1%.
THE GUESS of why it came out so: The scheduler share, not queue capacity or TCP congestion control, sets fa_goodput: lc.queue.parts.fa divides raw lc bits and packet-header overhead reduces the payload share, so increasing lc.queue.length leaves fa_goodput unchanged. The longer lc queue only changes drop selection by buffering more lc packets and reducing fb-related lc drops, lowering fb_loss_frac enough that the fb_loss_frac=0.1 boundary can move to a slightly higher parts.fa without changing fa_goodput.
THE HYPOTHESIS H9: At lc.queue.parts.fa=0.185, lc.queue.length=1000, fa.type=TcpCubic, fb_loss_frac <= 0.1.
DECISION RULE: fb_loss_frac@p0185_len1000 <= 0.1 AND fb_loss_frac@p0185_len1000 < fb_loss_frac@p0185

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.
